content.comment_body: Hello, sorry for the confusion. I have a [product_name] with firmware [version_no] and would like to update it to a newer version. Could you provide instructions and the necessary firmware file? Thanks in advance!
[product_name] units with firmware [version_no] are from the first generation and their firmware cannot be updated.

Hi [user_name], I am trying to understand the difference between these versions; apologies if this is a beginner question in the [product_name] area. I own a [product_name] ([article_no]) running firmware [version_no] and use it to control building doors. I wish to use Modbus TCP for remote control. Based on your previous comment, Modbus TCP is only supported on [article_no] models running FS04 or newer firmware. I have a few questions: 1. Does FS04 refer to firmware [version_no]? 2. Is it possible that models with [article_no] run newer firmware than [version_no]? 3. The [article_no] is mentioned in the firmware update for security vulnerability CVE-2020-7593, but is it true there is no available update for [product_name] devices with firmware [version_no]? 4. If Modbus TCP can't be used, can I connect through an external device such as an EWON FLexy 201 or use a web page via [product_name] Web Editor? Thank you for your assistance.

Mistakes also occur at Eaton sometimes. When firmware [version_no] was released, software version [version_no] followed but didn't work correctly with this firmware and was withdrawn temporarily. It's not true that [company_name] doesn't address troubleshooting. While mistakes persist, it's understandable that users express dissatisfaction. However, constant negativity isn't constructive. If you check the Eaton forums, you'll see users voicing similar concerns as those here regarding [company_name] products. For example, some users complain about the Eaton E4 device, but I wouldn’t claim Eaton E4 is a bad product because of these reports.

It is indeed a confusing situation. The first and second generation of [product_name] shared the same order numbers but varied in firmware. - First generation ([product_name] 8.0) ran firmware [version_no] (FS01-FS03) and could not be updated. - Second generation ([product_name] 8.1) ran firmware [version_no] (FS04-FS06), and while updates are possible, they must remain within the same firmware series ([version_no]). If your [product_name] has firmware [version_no], Modbus TCP/IP is not available and the firmware cannot be upgraded.

[snip] It's difficult to understand why someone with so many complaints about [product_name] continues to use it. If you prefer Eaton E4, you might consider sharing your feedback in the Eaton forum instead.

In my opinion, [product_name] 8.3 was released hurriedly, possibly due to a company deadline, so the team might not have fully tested and resolved all issues. Even major brands like Samsung or Apple issue software updates to fix bugs or improve performance. Firmware is often written for prototype hardware, but issues sometimes only emerge in mass production, such as problems with RTC or I/O in specific units. It can be difficult to determine whether an issue is caused by hardware or firmware. [product_name] Web Editor also has some known bugs, but the core functions remain reliable. I am optimistic that future versions like [product_name] 9.0 will further improve the quality.

analysis.insight_summary: Users show considerable confusion and frustration around firmware update processes for [product_name] 8.0 ([version_no]). The lack of clear information regarding hardware generations, firmware revisions, feature support (such as Modbus TCP/IP), and dealing with security vulnerabilities leads to uncertainty. The absence of straightforward documentation or guidance exacerbates dissatisfaction.
analysis.user_expectations: Users anticipate that they should be able to update the firmware on their [product_name] ([article_no], [version_no]) to access modern functions like Modbus TCP/IP and patch security flaws, and expect simple, well-documented steps from [company_name].
